questions.q_en:

The ability to impart knowledge and ______ respect is the essential qualification for teachers.
questions.solution_en:
A base verb would fit in the blank to follow parallelism with another base verb 'impart' placed before the conjunction 'and'. So, the noun 'disappearance' is eliminated. The sentence intends to convey that giving knowledge and respect is the basic requirement in any teacher. Since, 'respect' can be either given or received so the words 'improve' and worsen' cannot fit in. Thus, 'command(give)' is the correct choice.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Note:

Parallelism: In grammar, parallelism, also known as parallel structure or parallel construction, is a balance within one or more sentences of similar phrases or clauses that have the same grammatical structure. Given below is an example which shows a sentence in two forms (parallel in structure and lacking parallelism): Lacking parallelism: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and to sing. Parallel: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and singing.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rajan said to me, "I don't want to go into your house right now."
options_en: Rajan told me that he do not want to go into my house right then.
Rajan told me that he did not want to go into my house right then.
Rajan told me that he had not wanted to go into my house right now.
Rajan requested me that he wanted to go into my house right then.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· The verb 'do' (simple present) is changed into 'did' (simple past).

· The possessive determiner 'your' is changed into 'my'.

· 'Right now' is changed into 'right then'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Rajan told me that he did not want to go into my house right then.

B. Celsius and Fahrenheit use completely different measurements - for instance, water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, but 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

D. If you're interested in taking the temperature of something, there are two different units of measurement available to you: Celsius (or centigrade) and Fahrenheit.
questions.solution_en:

Sentence B follows the pair DC and states that Celsius and Fahrenheit use completely different measurements. A follows B as it talks about the common point where the two scales meet. 'However' is used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He had finished his homework before the party started.
options_en: His homework had finished by him before the party started.
His homework had been finished by him before the party started.
His homework has been finished by him before the party started.
His homework was being finished by him before the party started.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb [been] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + had + been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

I had called her. (Active Voice)

She had been called by me. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): His homework had been finished by him before the party started.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Hira inquired how I was doing being all alone in my house.
options_en: Hira said to me, "Are you doing fine being all alone in your house."
Hira said to me, "How are you doing being all alone in my house."
Hira said to me, "How are you doing being all alone in your house?"
Hira said to me, "How you are doing being all alone in your house?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the past continuous. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the present continuous.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· 'was doing' changes to 'are doing'.

· 'I' changes to 'you'.

· 'my' changes to 'your'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Hira said to me, "How are you doing being all alone in your house?"

questions.q_en:

Had you been to Dubai, I would also go with you.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence uses the third conditional ("Had you been... would have...") to describe a hypothetical past situation. The correct substitution should maintain this structure, so "I would have gone" is appropriate.

Option 1: Incorrect. "I shall be gone" is future tense and doesn't match the conditional structure.

Option 2: Incorrect. "I will have went" uses incorrect grammar ("went" should be "gone") and is future perfect, not conditional.

Option 3: Incorrect. "I would has also gone" uses incorrect grammar ("has" should be "have") and is not idiomatic.

The correct sentence is: Had you been to Dubai, I would have gone with you

Hence, the correct answer is option (4).

questions.solution_en:
The sentence indicates that the person has been working very hard and needs to relax and take a break. The idiom should reflect this need for rest and unwinding.

The missing phrase must idiomatically describe the act of relaxing and enjoying oneself after a period of hard work.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

If you ask me, success is about more than just ______ (A) growth and optimized productivity. It's about living by our values, or attributes of the person we want to be, which means making time for _______ (B) activities that match our values. And, as there are often not enough hours in the day, we must prioritize our list of values. Experimenting with short-term routines ______ (C) us determine which values are most important to us and whether an activity reflects them. We can drop misaligned short-term routines and hang on to relevant ones. That also helps our routines to evolve along with us as our lives change. A routine that worked for you 10 years ago may not apply to your environment and values now. Studies show that our personality _____ (D) as we age, evolving with our experiences.

Which of the following words can fill in the blank C?
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires a verb that denotes the thing that short-term routines do to us. Among the options, 'boils' (reach or cause to reach the temperature at which it bubbles and turns to vapour), 'believes' (accept that (something) is true, especially without proof) and 'narrates' (give a spoken or written account of) do not convincingly convey what the short-term routines do and so, they are negated. 'Helps' (be of benefit to) is the apt word that denotes what short-term routine does to us.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).
